courses.project: Professional portfolio: a design document, a postmortem, an ethics case analysis, a plan for contributing to an open-source project, and a one-year career growth plan, each written to the standard a senior engineer would expect.
courses.completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

Y.name: Young learner
Y.evidence: Gets most questions right again a week later and can show the idea with objects, drawings or a tiny program.

T.name: Theory
T.evidence: Two independent cumulative attempts near 85%, with sound reasoning and repaired prerequisites.

W.name: Reading and writing
W.evidence: A clear, supported piece of writing on an unseen prompt, and accurate analysis of an unseen text.

L.name: Laboratory science
L.evidence: Two cumulative attempts near 85%, plus a lab report with data, uncertainty and a defensible conclusion.

P.name: Programming
P.evidence: Two cumulative attempts near 85% on unseen problems, and a working, tested program you wrote yourself without copying it or having AI write it.

E.name: Engineering practice
E.evidence: A working project and written designs that a senior engineer would accept with small changes, plus near 85% on an unseen cumulative check.
